newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA bunkers crash, other areas trickle down.
newsitem.headline: ARA bunkers crash, other areas trickle down.

text.p: ARA bunker prices crashed on Wednesday as the barge market finally responded to tumbling crude, while bunkers in other ports weakened a little further, after sharp falls on Tuesday dealers said.
Rotterdam 380 cst fuel oil ended the session trading at around $114 fob, about $6 lower than at Tuesday's close, and some $3 down from early morning business.
Demand remained light as shipowners delayed all but essential purchases, believing further weakness was due.
"Lots of people have delayed their decisions, including many who were enquiring next week," said one supplier.
Hamburg also headed down, by a relatively modest $4. As in Rotterdam, numerous enquiries resulted in few trades.
Mediterranean buying was healthier, with prices up to $2 weaker.
Fujairah was 50 cents to $1 up. Demand was down after a Tuesday flurry of trade, but supply was also limited as two refiners were unprepared to offer until the second half of December.
Saudi Aramco cut bunker fuel by $2 to $125 in the Gulf and by $3 to $125 in the Red Sea.
